_comment: Known IPC registration gaps at gate introduction (F-008/F-050). Entries are UI command strings not yet registered in that shell; they shrink to zero as F-006 removes the dead surface. Stale entries (command now registered) fail the gate, and so does an entry this run cannot reproduce as a gap at all -- one no production UI code names and no shell registers, which exempts nothing and used to be reported as info[<shell>-unreachable] while the run still returned 0 (2026-09-18, unreproduced_entry_message in scripts/verify-ipc-parity.py). create_backup_scoped / get_backup_status_scoped joined with 5f0692e1: DataManagementScreen now prefers the permission-checked twins, but the tablet shell registers no data surface at all -- create_backup, get_backup_status, export_data, import_data and import_preview were already listed here. The unscoped names stay, because the ADR #7 conditional still falls back to them when no session token exists. pick_logo_file_scoped joined the same way: AppearanceSettings now prefers the SETTINGS_EDIT-checked twin, and the tablet shell registers neither variant. pause_subscription_scoped / resume_subscription_scoped joined the same way: LicenseSettings now prefers the SETTINGS_EDIT-checked twins, and the tablet shell registers neither variant of either command. get_report_schedule_scoped joined the same way: EmailReportSettings now prefers the REPORTS_SCHEDULE-checked twin, and the tablet shell registers neither variant. The legal-entity commands were initially allowlisted with bcd1f501 while the tablet shell had no implementation; they are removed from this list once the shared command module is registered in the tablet shell. The three memo-authoring entries (create_memo_scoped, list_authored_memos_scoped, publish_memo_scoped) are a deliberate product choice, not a gap: authoring is desktop-only (the back-office manager writes Memos; the tablet's Memo surface is the display banner), following the legal-entity precedent of desktop-first authoring IPC. stop_memo_scoped and revise_memo_scoped join them for the same reason (the 2026-09-07 A2/scope rulings): early-stopping and corrections are management actions on the authoring screen (MemosScreen is registry-gated to manager+ on desktop), and the tablet shell has no management surface. This was TRACED on 2026-10-25 rather than restated: list_authored_memos_scoped has a real caller (ui/src/features/memo/MemosScreen.tsx:162, reached through features/memo/register.tsx into registerAllFeatures at ui/src/features/index.ts:103, called by ui/src/App.tsx:8 on the desktop entry) and the desktop shell registers the command at apps/desktop-tauri/src/lib.rs:1827, so the desktop half is live rather than dead -- the entry is an asymmetry, not an orphan. The tablet shell resolves routes through the same page registry (ui/src/app/tablet/TabletAppShell.tsx:531 getPage(currentRoute)) and its entry also calls registerAllFeatures (ui/src/main.mobile.tsx:16), so if the command were registered the route would resolve; the exemption is the missing REGISTRATION at apps/mobile-tauri, which is the product ruling, not a missing caller. All five come off this list only if Memo authoring/management is ever ported to the tablet shell. The two §J quota-remediation commands (suspend_surplus_workspace_instances_scoped, recover_workspace_instances_scoped) joined on 2026-09-09 for the same reason the memo entries did, and by the route the scoped_orphans comment prescribes: they sat in scoped_orphans as permission checks guarding nothing until B1 gave them a caller in the shared over-quota card, and this shell does not register them. Quota remediation is a back-office owner action on a tenant-level view, so this is a recorded product choice and not a gap. They come off this list when the tablet shell registers them - and, per the same rule, they must never leave one list without appearing in another. The get/set_location_ticket_prefix_scoped pair re-joined the tablet allowlist 2026-09-10 after W7-A (c53eb4421) retired their scoped_orphans entries once the UI half landed: the retirement proved the pair was a desktop-only asymmetry, not dead callers - the desktop-only partial slice (fd047cbd5) registered desktop only because tablet has no locations command surface (D37), while the shared api invokes both commands from either shell. Registering them on tablet would invent a surface, so they are allowlisted here as a recorded product choice, the same route the memo authoring entries took. The KDS routing-rules pair (get_kds_routing_rules_scoped, save_kds_routing_rules_scoped) joined 2026-09-13 on the identical ticket-prefix route: they are the config surface of todo-kds-agents-1 (desktop b7ab48870/652f18494/f8b91e5be/a63fd08b6), the shared ui/src/api/kds.ts wrappers (bac53b849) are read by both shells' bundle, and the rules editor mounts in the desktop KDS hamburger panel only - registering the pair on tablet would invent a kitchen-config management surface the tablet shell does not have, so this is a recorded product choice, not a gap. They come off this list only if KDS rule authoring is ever ported to the tablet shell. edc_terminal_status_scoped joined the same day on the EDC lane's OWN precedent: the tablet allowlist has carried edc_refund, edc_sale, edc_terminal_status and edc_void since the gate's introduction - the tablet shell has no EDC command surface at all (its only edc code is a device-bootstrap list_active_edc_terminals call in lib.rs, not a registered command), and the unscoped twin was already a recorded choice, so the scoped twin was a straggler of the 26ffd89c1 EDC landing, not a new gap. Its stale scoped_orphans entry (the gate's own first violation: 'still registered in desktop and now has a caller') moved to the tablet list, which is where the exemption belongs; it comes off if the tablet ever registers an EDC surface. open_cash_drawer and print_receipt left BOTH shell lists on 2026-09-16: b8ba7c573 deleted the unscoped ui/src/api/hardware.ts wrappers, so no UI code names either command any more. Their dev-mock handlers DELIBERATELY STAY at ui/src/dev-mock/handlers/sync.ts:19-20, and that asymmetry is the point -- applyScopedAliases() (ui/src/dev-mock/core/mockDispatcher.ts) mirrors every registered unscoped handler onto its _scoped twin, and the UI now invokes only open_cash_drawer_scoped / print_receipt_scoped. Delete the unscoped stubs and the scoped names the screens actually call fall through to a silent null in browser dev preview (the R36-02 failure mode), so these two are mock-only alias sources rather than dead code. T21 (b2) 2026-09-17: list_scanners / start_scanner / stop_scanner left BOTH lists -- useBarcodeScanner.ts and useWarehouseScanner.ts dropped their no-session arms, so no UI names those commands any more and the gate reported all six entries reachable by neither direction. Their dev-mock handlers in ui/src/dev-mock/handlers/system.ts are KEPT on purpose: unlike lookup_by_barcode, whose scoped twin is an explicit key next to it in catalog.ts, these three have no explicit _scoped key anywhere in dev-mock, so applyScopedAliases is the only thing that answers list_scanners_scoped &c. in a browser preview -- they are alias seeds (T16/T40), not leftovers. Do not delete them without writing the explicit scoped handlers first. Round 41 2026-09-17: lookup_by_barcode left BOTH lists on the same evidence -- the last production caller was the second scanner hook's no-session arm, now deleted, so the name was reachable by neither direction (reported 1 of 12 and 1 of 140, both back to 0). Its dev-mock handler at ui/src/dev-mock/handlers/catalog.ts:304 went with it, which is safe HERE and was not safe for the scanner trio above: catalog.ts registers the scoped twin explicitly two lines below with a byte-identical body, so the unscoped key was redundant rather than a seed. 2026-09-18: list_categories and list_products left the desktop section and list_products left the tablet section on the strength of that same report, which is now a failure. All three were unreproduced in both derivations the gate prints -- the gap sweep (no production UI file names them: the screens call list_categories_scoped / list_products_scoped, and ui/src/api/hardware.ts-style unscoped wrappers are gone) and the registration inventories (the desktop registers neither unscoped name; the tablet registers list_categories unscoped at lib.rs:530 and only list_products_scoped, so its unscoped products command is one of the two f006 deletion candidates, defined in products.rs and wired to no door). Nothing on either side asked for the exemptions, so they were deletions rather than decisions, and the entry count went 11 -> 9 and 139 -> 138. The tablet's products.rs::list_products FUNCTION is untouched by this -- it is a Rust deletion candidate under F-006, a different register, and the gate still names it on every run. 2026-09-19: the avatar write pair (set_avatar_scoped, clear_avatar_scoped) joined on the memo-authoring route. The avatar feature (f49170d3d) registered its three commands desktop-only, but the shared renderer it also changed (ui/src/features/sales/PosScreen.tsx -> RestaurantMenu -> RestaurantSidebar) is mounted by this shell too (ui/src/app/tablet/TabletAppShell.tsx:232), so the parity gate reported three tablet violations. The READ was registered rather than allowlisted, because PosScreen calls get_own_avatar_scoped unconditionally on mount and registering it therefore completes an existing surface instead of inventing one -- before it, the tablet's restaurant sidebar header fell back to the initials tile for good, silently, since the call is wrapped in .catch(). The two WRITES would invent a surface: their affordance is the sidebar's Change photo, whose own string is restaurant-avatar-desktop-only (Changing your photo needs the desktop app), and this shell registers no dialog plugin (apps/mobile-tauri/Cargo.toml carries no tauri-plugin-dialog and its lib.rs no tauri_plugin_dialog::init(), unlike apps/desktop-tauri), so there is no file picker to choose an image with. They come off this list if the tablet ever gets a dialog plugin and an upload ruling. 2026-09-20: that condition is met -- the owner reversed the desktop-only ruling ("we want b-full"), tauri-plugin-dialog and tauri-plugin-fs were promoted to direct dependencies of the tablet shell and registered, and PickImage now bridges the content:// URI Android's picker returns into a real cache path (ui/src/api/file-bridge.ts). The two writes are therefore registered rather than exempted, and they leave this list; the string that used to justify their absence (restaurant-avatar-desktop-only) was replaced by image-pick-app-only, which excludes the browser dev preview rather than the tablet. The same pass registered export_data, import_preview, import_data and the product image pair (products_set_image_scoped, products_clear_image_scoped), so those five leave too -- the sentence above about "no data surface at all" no longer describes the shell. has_users leaves with them, having been registered by another lane. create_backup and get_backup_status (and their _scoped twins) STAY on purpose: they take no destination, so a tablet backup would land in private storage the operator cannot reach, and giving them one is a contract change to a command the desktop also calls -- an open owner decision recorded in todo-tablet-dialog-content-uri.md §3.3, not a gap this list should paper over. Tablet entries 140 -> 132. 2026-10-08: check_app_update, start_apk_download and prepare_and_launch_update joined the desktop section -- the Android in-app self-updater (9e298417b) registers all three on the tablet shell alone, since they stream an APK and hand off to the Android package installer, and no desktop implementation exists to register. This was a real C40-shaped defect, not a papered-over gap: the shared UpdateSettingsCard had no shell guard, so a desktop mount would have invoked all three and rendered its silent failure path (ipc parity's forward leg caught it; verify-scoped-reads caught the two call sites). Fixed at the call sites with the C47 idiom -- each invoke now sits inside if (isTabletShell()), with the card's mount in SystemDiagnosticsScreen gated too -- and these desktop entries record the remaining registration asymmetry the way the memo-authoring entries do, as a deliberate tablet-only surface. They come off this list if the Android updater is ever ported to the desktop shell. The three are bare names as this section requires; the reason lives here because scripts/verify-scoped-reads.py reads this section as command names.
_tablet_comment:
2026-10-25 (round 177): WHY THESE ARE BARE. This section holds 78 names and until today carried no rationale of any kind -- not per entry, and no "_tablet_comment" key. That is not an oversight in the file: a shell section MUST stay a list of bare command names, because scripts/verify-scoped-reads.py grades it by those names and refuses the object form there, while scripts/verify-ipc-parity.py refuses it too and names that first script as its reason (measured this round by feeding an object into the "tablet" section of a deep copy and reading allowlist_shape_problems). The two validators point at each other, so the object form is unavailable and prose is the only venue. This key is that prose.

THE MEASUREMENT. Each of the 78 names was resolved to the desktop module that registers it (regex over apps/desktop-tauri/src/lib.rs generate_handler, first registration wins) and cross-checked against the modules apps/mobile-tauri/src/lib.rs registers at all. All 78 resolve; the split below is why the list is long and why most of it is not a defect.

FIVE ENTIRE MODULES EXIST ONLY ON DESKTOP -- 21 of the 78, and the reason is a product decision about what a tablet is for, not a missing registration. The tablet registers 59 command modules; desktop-only are local_api, payables, security, topology and email. Their entries:
  topology (10) -- can_save_topology, apply_topology_diff, delete_topology_template, list_topology_revisions, list_topology_templates, load_topology, load_topology_revision, load_topology_template, pin_topology_revision, save_topology_template
  local_api (6) -- local_api_mint_token_scoped, local_api_rotate_secret_scoped, local_api_set_enabled_scoped, local_api_set_port_scoped, local_api_set_store_scoped, local_api_status_scoped
  payables (5) -- create_payable_scoped, list_payables_scoped, record_payable_payment_scoped, write_off_payable_scoped, get_ap_aging_report_scoped
  email (4) -- get_report_schedule, get_report_schedule_scoped, save_report_schedule, send_test_report
  security (1) -- get_key_rotation_info
Round 154 recorded the topology case in detail (todo-warehouse-tablet-command-gap.md, RULING 2): TopologyScreen returns a tablet notice before its JSX, so the calls are guarded and unreachable. Apex 175 attempted to teach verify-scoped-reads that shape and reverted, because the guard sits in the PARENT function of the component that owns the call.

THE REST, by owning module, with the reason they are here:
  workspaces (11) -- the topology workspace-instance surface: same desktop-only authoring decision as topology above, registered under a module the tablet does have. archive_workspace_instance_scoped, create_workspace_instance_scoped, get_user_workspace_instances_scoped, get_workspace_instance_scoped, list_workspace_screens_scoped, list_workspaces_for_store_scoped, list_workspaces_scoped, recover_workspace_instances_scoped, set_user_workspace_instances_scoped, suspend_surplus_workspace_instances_scoped, update_workspace_instance_scoped
  license (9) -- activate_license, pause_subscription, pause_subscription_scoped, renew_license, resume_subscription, resume_subscription_scoped, restore_prepare, restore_status, list_restore_candidates. Licensing and restore are owner-only back-office actions; the tablet registers no restore module. useRestore.ts:143 carries `const isAvailable = !isTabletShell() && sessionToken !== ''`, so the three restore reads never fire (round 174).
  data (7) -- create_backup, create_backup_scoped, get_backup_status, get_backup_status_scoped, get_machine_id, get_hardware_fingerprint, test_auth_connection. Backup destination differs per platform: useBackupStatus.ts:140 branches so the tablet calls create_backup_to and never reaches create_backup (it is in the "desktop" section instead).
  memo (5) -- create_memo_scoped, list_authored_memos_scoped, publish_memo_scoped, revise_memo_scoped, stop_memo_scoped. Memo AUTHORING is desktop-only by product choice (recorded in _scoped_orphans_comment); the tablet keeps the read side.
  sync (5) -- get_pg_sync_settings_scoped, pg_sync_start_scoped, pg_sync_status_scoped, pg_sync_stop_scoped, update_pg_sync_settings_scoped. Postgres sync is a server-side daemon control surface; no tablet UI.
  kds_device (4) -- deactivate_kds_device_scoped, get_kds_device_scoped, resolve_kds_targets_scoped, update_kds_device_status_scoped. KDS device provisioning is done from the admin surface.
  terminals (4) -- delete_terminal_profile_scoped, get_terminal_profile_scoped, list_terminal_profiles_scoped, set_terminal_profile_scoped. The whole terminal-PROFILE sub-family is unregistered on the tablet (round 174 measured this); the tablet registers nine other terminals:: commands, so this is a family gap, not a module gap.
  branding (2) -- pick_logo_file, pick_logo_file_scoped. A file picker is desktop chrome.
  kds_routing (1) -- save_kds_routing_rules_scoped. Rule authoring, same decision as memo authoring.
  edc (1) -- edc_terminal_status. EDC status polling is a desktop settings surface.
  browser (1) -- open_product_images_scoped. Not a gap at all: openProductImages in ui/src/api/browser.ts tests isTabletShell() first and only the desktop arm invokes the scoped twin (_desktop_comment records the mirror of this under the "desktop" section).
  products (1) -- list_warehouse_products_at_location. The desktop-only per-location warehouse read; RULING 2 withheld the Count mode on tablet instead of substituting the unfiltered twin (todo-warehouse-tablet-command-gap.md).
  adjust_stock (1) -- NOT a shell gap and not a registration: it resolves to no registration line in EITHER shell, because only its twin adjust_stock_scoped is registered (desktop lib.rs:1619, tablet lib.rs:1375). info[tablet-uinamed] classes it exactly: "named only by an api wrapper nothing imports (dead surface both sides, deletable; not a parity gap)". It is listed in this section because the section is keyed by UI command name, and that name has no door by design.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM. That every one of the 78 is correct. It claims that each has a reason of one of five kinds: a whole module the tablet does not have (21), a family gap inside a module it does have (terminals 4), a platform-specific twin that routes elsewhere (browser 1, backup 4), a product decision to keep authoring off the device (topology/workspaces/memo/kds_routing/license 33), or an unregistered-command tracker entry that belongs to another leg (adjust_stock 1). A lane that wants to retire any of them starts from the module list above, not from the bare names.

WHY NOT PER-ENTRY REASONS: the schema forbids it here, and that is enforced, not stylistic. Adding them requires either teaching verify-scoped-reads.py to read the object form in a shell section, or moving the reasons to a sidecar. Both are larger than this round and neither is obviously right -- a sidecar can drift from the list it describes, which is the failure this key exists to avoid.

scoped_orphans.name: check_license_status_scoped
scoped_orphans.reason: MEASURED 2026-10-25: session-validating twin with NO per-domain permission -- it calls ctx.resolve_session and delegates. That matches license/scoped.rs's own contract at :3-5 ("applies the per-domain permission (F-017) WHERE THE OPERATION MUTATES a credential or a subscription"); a read does not, so the absence is by design and not a hole. The UI calls the UNSCOPED 'check_license_status' (one production reference); this variant has none. Consequence for a reader: routing this caller through the scoped door would add NO authorisation, only a session check most callers already hold -- so the fix is retirement (F-006) or leaving it, not "use the gated one".

scoped_orphans.name: get_key_rotation_info_scoped
scoped_orphans.reason: MEASURED 2026-10-25, CORRECTED in round 155. The scoped twin IS gated (SECURITY_MANAGE). The unscoped twin is used by ui/src/hooks/useKeyAge.ts, and question (1) below has since been ANSWERED: the reminder DOES run. Round 147 mounted it -- components/KeyRotationReminder.tsx calls useKeyRotationReminder() and contexts/AppProviders.tsx:110 renders <KeyRotationReminder /> inside ToastProvider, so it is app-wide on both shells. That makes question (2) live and UNPAID: the mounted hook still calls the UNGATED unscoped door, because it takes no session token. The remedy is now a concrete edit rather than a decision -- give useKeyRotationReminder a session token and route it through getKeyRotationInfoScoped under the ADR #7 conditional. Until then a shell without SECURITY_MANAGE can read key age through the ungated door, which is exactly the narrowing this orphan entry records. NOTE: the earlier text said the hook was mounted nowhere; that was true when written and is not true now.

scoped_orphans.name: get_over_quota_report
scoped_orphans.reason: MEASURED 2026-10-25 (round 176): the AMBIENT arm of an ADR #7 pair whose SCOPED twin is the one in use -- api/subscription.ts:287 getOverQuotaReport invokes get_over_quota_report_scoped, called from OverQuotaCard.tsx:94, and this ambient arm has no caller. Both shells register both arms (desktop lib.rs:1757-1758, tablet lib.rs:1083-1084) and both carry the same settings:read gate; commands/subscription.rs:100-109 documents why the report scopes the session without opening a store (its dimensions are TENANT ceilings, not per-store ones). Not a retirement candidate and not a gap: it is the session-less arm of a pair the product does not use, and removing it is a decision about pre-session operation rather than cleanup. Recorded so info[cross-shell-reasons] stops reporting it as the one uncovered name.

scoped_orphans.reason: MEASURED 2026-10-25: this is a PERMISSION-GATED DUPLICATE, not a missing surface. pending_sync_count_scoped (crates/kasirmu-bridge/src/sync.rs:400 -- this entry cited pos.rs until 2026-10-25 round 176, and pos.rs contains no such function) and pending_offline_count_scoped both return the SAME value -- Store::pending_offline_count() -- and differ only in that this one requires SYNC_MANAGE while the other is ungated (its own 'ungated-ok: documented split' comment). The ungated twin has two production callers (OfflineQueueScreen, UpdateSettingsCard); this one has none and should not get one, because a UI that needs the count already has a door for it. Recorded rather than deleted: it is registered in BOTH shells and is an F-006 retirement candidate, not a gap to fill. The bare-name entry this replaces said nothing, which is how it survived three sweeps.

_scoped_orphans_comment: Scoped commands registered in a shell's generate_handler! that no client invokes, accepted as host-only. Each entry is a permission check that currently guards nothing, so this list is a work queue, not a clean bill of health. An entry that gains a caller fails the gate as stale. The memo authoring entries (create/publish/list_authored) are NOT host-only orphans — the authoring screen now invokes all three from the shared api (3fb745cf), so they left this list and moved to the tablet allowlist with a recorded product choice: authoring is desktop-only, following the legal-entity precedent. They return here only if tablet registration would leave them caller-less again. The four payables entries (create/list/record_payment/write_off) are the desktop-only AP authoring surface landed ahead of its UI: the Hutang screen is a later slice, so these commands currently have no caller at all (unlike memo authoring, which already has one). They leave this list when the payables UI wires them, exactly as the memo entries did. `list_security_events_scoped` left this list on 2026-09-09, when its caller landed in `ui/src/api/audit.ts` — it was never host-only, just early, and the exit condition recorded here is the one it met. It is NOT clean: the same command now sits under `dev_mock` because the browser mock still has no handler. Moving between these two lists is the honest bookkeeping; disappearing from both is not the same claim.
_dev_mock_comment: UI command strings that no handler anywhere under ui/src/dev-mock can answer -- the gate walks that whole tree since cb0175ce26 and reads tauri-api.ts as only its router, so a name listed here has no handler in tauri-api.ts OR in handlers/<domain>.ts and no unscoped twin for the alias rule (core/mockDispatcher.ts) to reach, so invoke() resolves to null in browser dev preview. That silent null is the R36-02 failure mode the mock itself warns about, so every entry here is recorded debt, not a clean pass. Entries appear when a slice adds a UI caller while dev-mock -- a hot file owned by another stream -- has no handler yet; the gap is recorded rather than editing that file. An entry fails the gate as stale the moment a handler appears, which is what makes the list self-clearing. list_role_holders_scoped was the first entry here — added 2026-09-08 with the role-holders slice, when the command was registered and gated (staff:read) in both shells with a live caller and no mock — and cleared 2026-09-09 once dev-mock gained its handler. It is the only entry that has ever self-cleared, which is the point of the staleness check: an entry that outlives its gap makes the gate lie in the other direction. list_security_events_scoped joined 2026-09-09 with the audit security-events UI half, and is the SAME command moving lists rather than new debt: it left scoped_orphans the day its caller landed, so the remaining gap is only the browser mock. Note what its null resolved to there, because it was not benign in the way an empty list would be — the backend refuses a Free tier outright, so a browser preview could not distinguish tier refusal from a transport failure and would always show the failure path. It cleared on 2026-09-09 with SecurityTrailScreen: the handler returns a plausible page and honors the outcome and query args, so the preview exercises the same filtering the real command does server-side. What the list still cannot see is a handler with the WRONG SHAPE. export_audit_log_scoped returned an empty string to an object DTO and mark_audit_reviewed_scoped returned null to one; get_audit_review_status_scoped was NOT a shape violation (its checkpoint/unreviewed_count pair matched AuditReviewStatusDto exactly) but was inert, hard-coding a null checkpoint and a zero count so a review could never be previewed. All three were corrected 2026-09-09 and are pinned by ui/src/__tests__/dev-mock-audit-shapes.test.ts against the Rust field names rather than against the mock. That test also caught a subtler sibling of the same class: invoke() hands a handler args?.['args'] ?? args, so a handler that reads args.args receives nothing and silently ignores every filter — list_security_events_scoped did exactly that when it was written here, under a comment claiming it honored them. A mock can therefore lie about its OUTPUT, its INPUT, or its INERTNESS, and this gate has only ever been asked about absence.
